annotations.title: Find the eclipses near a date

description:
Finds the solar and lunar eclipses nearest a date: greatest eclipse to the second in UTC, type, obscuration, the eclipsed body's sign, days from the date, and for a solar eclipse where greatest eclipse meets the Earth. Given a place, each listing also carries what that observer gets: local kind, first contact, maximum, last contact and altitude at each.

The 6,585.3-day saros groups eclipses into families whose members fall about a year or a continent apart, and a global eclipse is seen from only part of the Earth. Global and local circumstances are kept apart, including the Moon setting partway through or rising with the eclipse underway.

Results include an attribution line and a permalink.

count.description: How many per side of the date, "1" to "12", default "3". Example: "1". Each extra one adds server time.

date.description: The date to search around, ISO YYYY-MM-DD, 1700-2200. Example: "2026-08-12". Defaults to today (UTC).

family.description: Which eclipses to list: "both" (the default), "lunar" or "solar".

lat.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "64.1466". Paired with lon.

lon.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "-21.9426". Paired with lat.

place.description: Observer town or city. Example: "Reykjavik, Iceland". Adds the local kind, contact times and altitudes.

tz.description: IANA zone or numeric UTC offset hours for the local contact times. Example: "Atlantic/Reykjavik".

name: find_eclipses
